answer: The sparrow test I would run is Clinical trial participation record with ethics approval: a trial joined under an ethics approval, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because a trial joined under an ethics approval is bound to a single identity — the voyage is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the bridge of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
